properties.markdown:
# Contact-centre KPIs — Nexora / Ava
Rates, resolution and unit cost. Ledger integrity, token detail and the raw account bill live on **[Ava-Observability](/cloudwatch/home?region=us-west-2#dashboards/dashboard/Ava-Observability)**.

Two ways of counting, kept apart on purpose, because they answer different questions and are *allowed* to disagree: the **connection view** (`call.ledger` EMF metrics, ~1 min) asks how the connection ended; the **need view** (`case.summarized`, minutes later, a model reads the transcript) asks whether the caller got what they rang for. A caller who got their answer and hung up satisfied leaves a socket identical to an abandoned one — so **the abandonment tile is an upper bound** and the need view further down is the figure to quote.

Trends are plotted **daily**. Sub-daily buckets at the current call volume are mostly empty and read as an outage rather than as a quiet afternoon. Widen the time range at the top right and the charts stay daily; change the period per widget if volume grows.

properties.title: Calls
Success rate

properties.markdown:
## Counting from zero — reset 2026-09-14T12:12:19.000Z
**This dashboard is zeroed at the timestamp above and counts nothing before it.** The window is absolute and open-ended, so it is always "everything since the reset" and every widget started at 0.

That was the point of resetting: **every instrument was already live before this moment** — `call.ledger` since 09-11, `call.teardown` since 09-11 11:38, `case.written` / `case.summarized` since the 09-14 08:48 deploy. So the three counts below are now measuring the same population and **should agree**.

Which makes this section an alarm rather than an excuse. Before the reset a short count meant "instrumented later"; from here it cannot. **If `call.ledger` trails `call.teardown` now, calls are losing their ledger** — they happened, cost money, and appear in no metric. That is a live bug, not a coverage artifact. Two calls did exactly this on 09-14 (`9a7708f746c0`, `abc63b434f8f`); `Ava-LedgerLost` is built to catch it and has never been applied.

Widening the range at the top right still shows the older data — CloudWatch metrics cannot be deleted, only aged out — so nothing has been destroyed, and the pre-reset history stays one click away.

properties.title: Coverage — how many calls each source can see
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event in ["call.teardown","call.ledger","case.written","case.summarized"]
| stats count(*) as records by event
| sort records desc

properties.title: When each source started — a line that begins late was instrumented late
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event in ["call.teardown","call.ledger","case.written","case.summarized"]
| stats count(*) as records by bin(1d), event

properties.title: Is the cost complete? — priced vs unpriced, by how usage was read
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "call.ledger"
| stats count(*) as calls,
        sum(cost_priced) as priced,
        count(*) - sum(cost_priced) as unpriced,
        sum(CallCostUsd) as total_usd,
        avg(CallCostUsd) as avg_usd,
        sum(CallCostUsd)*60/sum(CallDurationSeconds) as usd_per_talk_min
    by usage_mode
| sort calls desc

properties.markdown:
## Escalation, engagement and quality proxies
`escalated`, `transcript_turns` and `tool_errors` are **fields on the `call.ledger` line, not CloudWatch metrics** — the EMF block publishes only Calls, duration, tokens, tool calls, gate blocks and cost. So these are Logs Insights queries: retroactive over log retention, but they cannot be alarmed on. Promoting them means adding to the `metrics` list in `emit_call_ledger`.

properties.title: Escalation — asking for a human vs getting one
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "call.ledger"
| stats count(*) as calls,
        sum(escalated) as escalated,
        sum(escalated)*100.0/count(*) as escalation_rate_pct,
        sum(human_handoff) as human_joined,
        sum(human_handoff)*100.0/count(*) as handoff_rate_pct,
        sum(escalated) - sum(human_handoff) as queued_never_joined

properties.title: Engagement — did the caller get past hello
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "call.ledger"
| fields greatest(least(transcript_turns - 1, 1), 0) as engaged,
         least(ToolCalls, 1) as transacted
| stats count(*) as calls,
        sum(engaged)*100.0/count(*) as engagement_rate_pct,
        sum(transacted)*100.0/count(*) as transacted_rate_pct,
        sum(transcript_turns)/count(*) as avg_turns,
        sum(ToolCalls)/count(*) as avg_tool_calls,
        avg(CallDurationSeconds) as aht_secs

properties.title: Quality proxies — NOT a quality score (see foot of dashboard)
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "call.ledger"
| fields least(GateBlocks, 1) as hit_gate, least(tool_errors, 1) as hit_tool_error
| stats count(*) as calls,
        sum(GateBlocks)/count(*) as gate_blocks_per_call,
        sum(hit_gate)*100.0/count(*) as calls_with_gate_block_pct,
        sum(tool_errors)/count(*) as tool_errors_per_call,
        sum(hit_tool_error)*100.0/count(*) as calls_with_tool_error_pct

properties.title: Escalation and engagement trend, by day
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "call.ledger"
| fields greatest(least(transcript_turns - 1, 1), 0) as engaged,
         least(ToolCalls, 1) as transacted
| stats sum(escalated)*100.0/count(*) as escalation_pct,
        sum(human_handoff)*100.0/count(*) as handoff_pct,
        sum(engaged)*100.0/count(*) as engagement_pct,
        sum(transacted)*100.0/count(*) as transacted_pct
    by bin(1d)

properties.markdown:
## Need view, and first contact resolution
From `case.summarized` / `case.written` — written only after a model reads the transcript, so these trail the tiles above and cover fewer calls (see coverage, above). `customer_intent` and `resolution_status` are closed sets (`cases.py`), which is what makes them countable at all.

A `not recorded` slice is **not a resolution category** — it is a case whose log line predates the field. `case.summarized` gained `resolution_status`, `derived_status`, `caller_need_met` and `upgraded` in a deploy on 2026-09-14 around 08:48; rows written before it carry only `case_id` and `customer_intent`. Those rows are counted (they are real calls) and labelled, never silently dropped.

Every rate here is `sum(x)/count(*)`, never `avg(x)`. Logs Insights' `avg` skips rows where the field is absent while `count(*)` keeps them, so `avg` on a partly-populated field silently shrinks its own denominator — it read 60% where 3 of 7 cases were resolved, because only 5 rows carried the field. `rows_judged` next to `cases` is how you see that gap rather than infer it.

**FCR is shown as two halves and deliberately not averaged into one number.** *Resolved on the call* is the transcript's judgement (`caller_need_met`). *No repeat contact* is whether that policy rang again — and since Logs Insights cannot nest aggregations, it is reported as `unique policies ÷ contacts`, with the offending policies listed beside it. A call can pass the first and fail the second; true FCR needs both.

properties.title: Resolution mix — need view
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "case.summarized"
| stats count(*) as calls by coalesce(resolution_status, "not recorded") as resolution
| sort calls desc

properties.title: Intent mix — what callers rang about
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "case.summarized"
| stats count(*) as calls by coalesce(customer_intent, "not recorded") as intent
| sort calls desc

properties.title: FCR half 1 — resolved on the call, and how often the transcript overruled the socket
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "case.summarized"
| stats count(*) as cases,
        count(caller_need_met) as rows_judged,
        sum(caller_need_met) as resolved_on_call,
        sum(caller_need_met)*100.0/count(*) as resolved_on_call_pct,
        sum(upgraded) as upgraded,
        sum(upgraded)*100.0/count(*) as upgraded_pct

properties.title: FCR half 2 — repeat contact rate (ringing twice fails FCR however well each call went)
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "case.written" and ispresent(policy_id)
| stats count(*) as contacts,
        count_distinct(policy_id) as unique_policies,
        count(*) - count_distinct(policy_id) as repeat_contacts,
        100.0*count_distinct(policy_id)/count(*) as first_contact_pct,
        100.0*(count(*) - count_distinct(policy_id))/count(*) as repeat_contact_pct

properties.title: Who rang more than once — the calls FCR is losing to
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "case.written" and ispresent(policy_id)
| stats count(*) as contacts,
        earliest(@timestamp) as first_contact,
        latest(@timestamp) as last_contact,
        earliest(resolution_status) as first_outcome,
        latest(resolution_status) as last_outcome
    by policy_id
| filter contacts > 1
| sort contacts desc
| limit 50

properties.title: Connection view vs need view — every disagreement, with its intent
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "case.summarized"
| stats count(*) as calls by coalesce(derived_status, "not recorded") as connection_view,
                            coalesce(resolution_status, "not recorded") as need_view,
                            coalesce(customer_intent, "not recorded") as intent
| sort calls desc
| limit 50

properties.markdown:
## Cost — three different numbers, and you must not add them up
| Layer | Metric | What it is | Lag |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Per call** | `Ava/Calls CallCostUsd` | Nova Sonic, priced from the call's own token counts | ~1 min |
| **Per service** | `Ava/Cost DailyCostUsd` by `category` | what AWS actually **billed** | ~3 days |
| **Runtime compute** | AgentCore usage logs | vCPU/GB-hours a session held open — on Ava-Observability | ~1 min |

`ModelProduction` in the breakdown **is the same money as `CallCostUsd`**, counted the other way round: our estimate from tokens versus the bill. `cost_categories.py` says so in `CATEGORIES` (`"ledger: CallCostUsd"`). Adding them double-counts; comparing them is the monthly reconciliation (`reconcile.py`).

No cost tile fills a gap with zero. An unpriced range reads **No data**, never $0.00 — and if the coverage widget shows any `unpriced` calls, every figure here is understated, because cost averages over priced calls while `Calls` counts all of them.

properties.title: Model cost (range)
Cost per call (avg)
Cost per call (p90)
Cost per successful call
Cost per talk minute
AWS billed — latest settled day
Cost per call by day — unit economics
Cost per call by outcome — a handed-off call is not priced like a contained one
Cost breakdown by service — latest settled day (USD, ~3-day lag)
AWS cost by service, daily (stacked) — plotted when learned, ~3 days after the spend
Cost of each call — most recent first
properties.query:
SOURCE '/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/ava_voice_agent-TVSWmk7feq-DEFAULT'
| filter event = "call.ledger"
| fields CallCostUsd*60/CallDurationSeconds as usd_per_min
| fields @timestamp, call_id, outcome, escalated,
         CallDurationSeconds as secs, CallCostUsd as usd, usd_per_min,
         InputTokens as tok_in, OutputTokens as tok_out,
         ToolCalls as tools, usage_mode, cost_priced
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 50

properties.markdown:
## Average quality score — not measured yet
**There is no live quality score in this system, and nothing on this dashboard is a substitute for one.** The proxies above measure *discipline* — did grounding gates fire, did tools fail — not whether the call was any good.

The only quality apparatus that exists is `evals/golden/`: 40 hand-written cases graded by an LLM judge against a rubric. That is an **offline, pre-ship regression gate** for prompt edits — it scores a fixed set before deploy, not real calls after, and cannot fill this widget.

A real score needs a judge reading production transcripts at teardown and publishing `QualityScore` through `emit_call_ledger`: per-call model cost, added teardown latency, and a sampling decision. That is a feature, not a widget.
